entries.name: Puma
entries.migrates: no; home ranges shift with deer movements
behaviour: solitary ambush hunter of steep, broken country
covers kills with debris and returns to feed over several nights
males hold huge territories; kittens stay with the mother up to 2 years

voxel_model.pattern: tawny uniform coat, black-tipped tail and ear backs

entries.notes: The widest-spread land mammal in the Americas; in low-mountain country it is the apex predator to build around, not a pack animal.

entries.name: Bezoar goat (wild goat)
behaviour: steep rocky-slope specialist of low, dry mountains
bucks have long backward-sweeping scimitar horns
ancestor of every domestic goat

voxel_model.pattern: sandy-brown with dark dorsal stripe, light belly, black beard

entries.notes: Domesticated around 10,000 years ago alongside cereals; the design origin of the game's goats.

entries.name: Chukar
behaviour: lives in coveys on dry rocky slopes and canyon walls
explosive whirring flight, then prefers to run and scramble uphill
iconic upland game bird from the Balkans to India

voxel_model.pattern: sandy-grey back, black gorget and flank bars, white throat, red bill and legs

entries.notes: Incubates about 23 days. The quintessential partridge of low, stony ground; introduced as game worldwide.

entries.name: Grey goral
behaviour: stocky goat-antelope of low Himalayan rocky slopes
grizzled grey coat with a dark dorsal stripe
lies motionless to vanish on cliff ledges

voxel_model.pattern: grizzled grey, dark dorsal stripe, pale throat patch and bib

entries.notes: Prefers lower, scrubbier Himalayan ridgelines than the tahr; a foothill specialist filling the same niche as the chamois.

entries.name: Japanese serow
behaviour: solitary, territorial goat-antelope of Honshu's steep forested hills
preorbital glands exude a vinegar-smelling secretion
protected as a Special Natural Monument; revived from near-extinction

voxel_model.pattern: mottled black-grey-white shaggy coat, whitish cheeks and throat

entries.notes: Japan's flagship hill animal; appears on the 50-yen stamp and is sacred in local folklore.

entries.name: Nilgiri tahr
entries.migrates: altitudinal, follows rain between shola pockets
behaviour: state animal of Tamil Nadu; lives in herds on cliffs and shola-grassland edges
called the 'cliff goat'; the only species in its genus
endangered, a few thousand survive in the Western Ghats

voxel_model.pattern: dark brown, pale shaggy mane on males, short ridged horns

entries.notes: Flagship of the Western Ghats; about half the wild population lives in Eravikulam National Park.

entries.name: Sambar
entries.migrates: altitudinal and seasonal, following water and forage
behaviour: largest deer in the foothill zone; wallows in mud and streams
stags roar and parallel-walk in the rut
key prey of tigers; raids hill crops at night

voxel_model.pattern: dark brown, shaggy mane, pale rump patch

entries.notes: The workhorse deer of tropical foothill forests; where sambar are abundant, tigers do well.

entries.name: Dhole
entries.migrates: follows prey movements over wide ranges
behaviour: pack-hunters of hill forest that run prey down in relays
whistle-like calls instead of howls
clan raises pups communally in denning holes

voxel_model.pattern: rust-red above, dark muzzle, white throat and tail tip

entries.player: dangerous; huntable (protected in parts of range)
entries.notes: Called the whistling dog; one of Asia's most efficient pack predators, often scavenging from tiger kills.

entries.name: Red junglefowl
behaviour: wild ancestor of the domestic chicken
males crow at dawn and hold loose harems
roosts in low trees; flees uphill on foot

voxel_model.pattern: male: orange-red neck hackles, dark green tail; female mottled brown

entries.notes: Incubates about 20 days. Every chicken in the world descends from this bird; an easy tell of foothill habitat.

entries.name: Indian peafowl
behaviour: males fan the long ocellated train in courtship
feral from India to the Mediterranean
roosts high in trees at night, calls at dawn and dusk

voxel_model.pattern: iridescent blue neck, eyespotted green-gold train; female drab brown

entries.notes: Incubates about 28 days. National bird of India; one of the loudest animals in any foothill village at dusk.

entries.name: Gray fox
behaviour: the only North American fox that climbs trees, using retractable claws
dens in rock crevices and hollow logs of low hills
more arboreal than the red fox; forages in canyon country

voxel_model.pattern: salt-and-pepper grey above, rust neck and flanks, black dorsal tail stripe

entries.notes: The fox of rocky canyon country; easily told from the red fox by its tree-climbing and black-striped tail.

entries.name: Chacma baboon
behaviour: troops sleep on cliffs and descend to forage at dawn
males yawn to flash long canine teeth in threat
raids orchards and maize; notorious around Cape towns

voxel_model.pattern: dark grey-brown, black face skin, pale rump in some populations

entries.notes: Troops of 30-50 move like sentient landslides through the kopjes; a real problem animal around South African farms.

entries.name: Rock hyrax
behaviour: colonial, basking on sun-warmed kopjes all day
closest living relative of the elephants
shrieks a sharp whistle alarm; fills the kopje with colonies

voxel_model.pattern: coarse dark fur, dorsal scent gland (cream spot), flat-backed body

entries.notes: Fills the small-mammal role on bare rock everywhere from Ethiopia to the Negev; an elephant relative the size of a guinea pig.

entries.name: Klipspringer
entries.migrates: no; home ranges fixed to rock outcrops
behaviour: stands on cylinder-like tiptoe hooves for grip on bare rock
lifelong monogamous pairs bound between kopjes
alarm whistle in duet; one partner always on watch

voxel_model.pattern: hollow air-filled golden coat, white chin and underparts, upright spike horns

entries.notes: The signature animal of African rocky kopjes; its modified hooves are unique among artiodactyls.

entries.name: Steenbok
behaviour: smallest antelope of the small-mountain zone; freezes, then bolts
distinctive ear tufts and tear-line gland marks
does not flee far; has drawn eagles away from fawns

voxel_model.pattern: chestnut-tawny coat, white chin and belly, bold pale ear fringes

entries.notes: The dik-dik of the Karoo foothills; a mainstay of small-game hunting.

entries.name: Common duiker
behaviour: sharp forehead ridge between the horns; dives and zig-zags when flushed
forages edge of scrub and rocky slopes
mostly solitary; territory marked with preorbital glands

voxel_model.pattern: grizzled grey-brown, rufous rump tuft, dark dorsal crest

entries.notes: Africa's most widespread small antelope; the default bushmeat quadruped of kopje and thicket.

entries.name: Bushbuck
entries.migrates: no; tames and habituates near water
behaviour: streaked and spotted; vanishes into cover along stream lines
males have spiralled horns, white mane and throat fringe
startles into a whistling dash rather than long flight

voxel_model.pattern: chestnut with white spots and stripes in rows, white mane and fringe

entries.notes: The classic sitatunga relative of broken, wet low hills; tame enough in parks to be a nuisance.

entries.name: Grey rhebok
entries.migrates: altitudinal, follows rain on the highveld
behaviour: woolly grey coat against cold high plateaus
rocking-horse bounding gait
males fight savagely at rut; territorial

voxel_model.pattern: soft woolly grey, pale underparts, bulbous dark nose, upright spike horns

entries.notes: Namesake of the Reebok shoe brand; near-threatened by habitat loss on the highveld.

entries.name: Cape mountain zebra
entries.migrates: altitudinal, down to valleys in dry winter
behaviour: smallest zebra; bold gridiron rump pattern and large dewlap
stallions herd a few mares on steep broken slopes
poached to near-extinction in the 1930s, now recovering in parks

voxel_model.pattern: dense narrow black stripes; stripes run to hooves; gridiron rump

entries.notes: Fewer than 3,000 survive; fell below 50 animals in the 1930s before Mountain Zebra National Park was founded in 1937.

entries.name: Lanner falcon
behaviour: hunts on the wing at kopjes and cliff faces
nests on ledges; prises clutches of rock-nesting birds
favoured by Arab falconers for its speed and style

voxel_model.pattern: slate-grey crown and back, rufous nape, pale streaked underparts

entries.player: not huntable; protected in parts of range
entries.notes: A fast, agile generalist falcon of rocky country from Italy to the Cape; popular with traditional falconers.

entries.name: Short-toed snake eagle
entries.migrates: summer visitor to Europe; resident in Africa and India
behaviour: hovers over hot rocky slopes to spot snakes, then stoops low to strike
swallows snakes whole, head first
favours open scrub with scattered trees for nesting

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown above, white below, barred flanks, large yellow eyes

entries.notes: Incubates about 45 days. Snakes are ~80% of its diet; it can swallow a 1.2 m snake whole.

entries.name: Wedge-tailed eagle
entries.migrates: no; nomadic following kangaroo and rabbit plagues
behaviour: Australia's largest raptor; wedge-shaped tail in flight
pairs reuse huge stick eyries on cliff ledges for decades
soars over hill country hunting kangaroos and lambs

voxel_model.pattern: dark golden-brown, rufous hackle in adults, pale-streaked juveniles

entries.notes: Wingspan over 2.3 m; one of the world's most powerful eagles, persecuted historically as a lamb-killer.

entries.name: Red-necked wallaby
behaviour: loose mobs graze grassy hill and forest-edge meadows
red neck and shoulders on a grey body; black nose
mob members bolt upright and bound away in unison

voxel_model.pattern: grey body, rufous neck and shoulders, pale face stripes

entries.notes: Gestation is only ~30 days followed by ~9 months in the pouch; very common in the Australian hills.

entries.name: Common brushtail possum
behaviour: noisy, bold rooftop and hill-forest climber
prehensile bushy tail; dens in hollow trees and roof cavities
major conservation pest in New Zealand

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown back, dark dorsal line, pink nose

entries.notes: Introduced to New Zealand in 1837; devoured native forests and is trapped and shot there at scale.

entries.name: Coastal carpet python
behaviour: sits in wait on branches and rafters over rodent runs
fully non-venomous constrictor; climbs and swims well
colonises rock ledges, roof voids and rock piles in hill country

voxel_model.pattern: olive with irregular yellow blotches edged in black, 'carpet' reticulation

entries.player: not huntable; protected in much of range
entries.notes: Incubates about 60 days and broods her clutch by shivering. A harmless, heavy snake that often finds its way into bush shacks.

entries.name: Red-legged seriema
behaviour: ground-runner of open scrubby hill country; rarely flies
kills prey by slamming it against rocks
pairs duet in long loud yowling calls at dawn and dusk

voxel_model.pattern: sandy barred plumage, bright red legs and bill, stiff frontal crest

entries.notes: Incubates about 30 days. Living relative of the terror birds; the call sounds like a puppy yelping and carries a mile.

entries.name: Rufous hornero
behaviour: builds a sealed mud-oven nest on fence posts and walls; national bird of Argentina
forages on the ground with tail cocked, like a wagtail
pairs duet from dawn to dusk

voxel_model.pattern: rufous above, white throat streaked, pale belly

entries.notes: Incubates about 16 days. Its mud oven outlasts the nest-builders and can stand for years.

entries.name: Red-billed chough
behaviour: acrobatic aerial displays over sea cliffs and grazed hill slopes
probes soil on short-grazed pasture
Cornwall's emblem; colonial nester in crevices

voxel_model.pattern: glossy black with red curved bill and red legs

entries.player: not huntable; protected in Britain and Ireland
entries.notes: Incubates about 19 days; a symbol of rugged coast and hill-grazing country needing short turf.

entries.name: Eurasian crag martin
behaviour: cliff-nesting swallow; colonies under limestone overhangs and old bridges
slow, bat-like flight with flashing white tail spots
often nests beside roads and buildings on warm hillsides

voxel_model.pattern: brown-grey above, paler throat, white spots on spread tail

entries.notes: Incubates about 15 days. The swallow most likely to nest on a cottage eave in rocky country.

entries.name: Alpine accentor
entries.migrates: altitudinal, descends to low cliffs in winter
behaviour: sparrow-like bird that shuffles over bare rock and scree
polyandrous and polygynandrous; unusually tangled mating system
winter flocks form on sheltered lee cliffs

voxel_model.pattern: streaked brown above, bold white-black throat patch, rufous wing panel

entries.notes: Incubates about 14 days. Found nearly year-round on European and Asian rock faces below the snowline.

entries.name: Wallcreeper
entries.migrates: altitudinal, clinging to rock faces year-round
behaviour: creeps up cliffs like a nuthatch; crimson-and-white wing-flashes in flight
nests in deep cliff crevices, lining with feathers and moss
rare winter wanderer as low as quarries and old buildings

voxel_model.pattern: slate-grey body, crimson wing panels with white spots, black forehead in female

entries.player: not huntable; protected in parts of range
entries.notes: Incubates about 13 days. A magical bird for rock climbers; almost nobody sees one without binoculars.

entries.name: Black redstart
entries.migrates: partial; short-distance elevation and latitude shifts
behaviour: quivers rust-orange tail constantly, perched on walls and crags
often nests on buildings in hill towns
thin wiry song from a high exposed perch

voxel_model.pattern: male: sooty black with rust tail and white wing panel; female grey-brown

entries.notes: Incubates about 13 days. The commonest redstart of cliffs, quarries and alpine buildings.

entries.name: European nightjar
entries.migrates: summer visitor to Europe; winters in sub-Saharan Africa
behaviour: sits camouflaged on the ground by day; churring song at dusk
aerial hawk of moths over heath and open hill
white wing spots flash in flight like a huge moth

voxel_model.pattern: mottled grey-brown, cryptic barring, white wing and tail spots

entries.notes: No nest to speak of; lays two eggs on bare ground. Declining with loss of open hill grazing.

entries.name: Woodlark
behaviour: sings from soaring flutter, then glides down on quivering wings
prefers sunny slopes with scattered trees and bare ground
a UK Biodiversity Action species; sparse in Britain

voxel_model.pattern: streaked sandy-brown, bold white supercilium, rufous-edged flight feathers

entries.notes: Incubates about 14 days. Needs bare ground mosaics; vanished from much of lowland Europe.

entries.name: Rock pigeon
behaviour: wild ancestor of every domestic and feral pigeon
nests in cliff crevices; thrives on bridges, towers and ledges
homing ability used by message pigeons for centuries

voxel_model.pattern: blue-grey with two black wing bars, white rump, iridescent green-purple neck

entries.notes: Incubates about 17 days. Feral populations everywhere trace back to this cliff-nesting hill bird.

entries.name: Nose-horned viper
entries.migrates: no; hibernation dens shared in winter
behaviour: distinctive soft horn on the snout tip
gives birth to live young
the most dangerous viper in Europe; shy but potent

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown with dark zigzag dorsal chevrons, pale flank spots

entries.notes: One of Europe's two most venomous snakes (with the adder and asp); bites are rare but serious.

entries.name: European green lizard
behaviour: males turn turquoise on head and flanks in spring
long-tailed runner of sunny stone slopes and walls
females retain a brown-green stripe

voxel_model.pattern: male brilliant green with blue throat; back spotted gold; very long tail

entries.player: not huntable; protected in parts of range
entries.notes: One of the largest lizards in Europe; a prized sight on sunny vineyard terraces and dry hill walls.

entries.name: Alpine newt
entries.migrates: short spring migration to breeding ponds
behaviour: breeds communally in cold ponds late into the season
males flash cobalt flanks with black spots to court
terrestrial most of the year under stones and logs

voxel_model.pattern: blue-black with paired rows of orange or black spots; orange belly with dark spots

entries.notes: Larvae wriggle like little fish; eggs are folded singly into submerged leaves. Amphibian of foothill ponds across central Europe.

entries.name: Rosalia longicorn

breeding.season: summer mating; larvae live 2-3 years in dead beech

behaviour: one of Europe's most beautiful beetles; sky-blue with black eyebrow spots
long antennae banded blue and black; males with far longer antennae
depends on ancient beech stands with sunlit dead wood

voxel_model.pattern: powder-blue with black thorax and paired black eyebrow-shaped elytral spots

entries.player: not huntable; strictly protected (EU Habitats Directive)
entries.notes: An indicator of old hill beech forest; its larvae take 2-3 years to develop in standing dead wood.
